summary.title: A Case for (Partially) TAgged GEometric History Length Branch Prediction
summary.one_liner: A research paper on TAGE-style branch predictors, which combine tagged tables indexed by geometric history lengths, and on the limits of what such predictors can learn.
keywords: branch predictor tables indexed by history
takeaways: TAGE-style predictors use several tagged tables indexed by geometric history lengths.
The paper frames this design as the one shipped processor predictors converge on.
It discusses what the geometric-history tagged predictor can and cannot learn.
summary.summary: This is a paper from the Journal of Instruction-Level Parallelism (volume 8, paper 1) on TAGE, the TAgged GEometric history length branch predictor. The paper's title and listing describe it as defining the tagged geometric-history predictor that shipped designs converge on, and the limits of what it can learn. The extracted page text is largely garbled symbol-encoded content, so the detailed methods, equations, and experimental results could not be reliably read and are not summarized here.
